title: Screening Whole Proteome of Aedes aegypti for In-Silico Molecular Interaction Studies
author: Chandrashekar K
materials: Molecular dynamic simulations for best docked complexes Protein-ligand binding induces alterations in the structure of the proteins and may cause changes in the stability of the docked complexes. At times, the ligand bound to the protein may dissociate from it during simulation due to its binding instability. To assess the stability of the docked complexes, a molecular dynamic simulation was carried out at 100ns for the top three complexes with least binding energies. This was performed using Maestro workspace in Desmond, by Schrodinger, that is known for its high reliability, scalability, accuracy, precision and rapidity. The simulations are performed in a realistic manner, mimicking the real-world scenarios/environments to evaluate the docked complex stability at specific conditions. Top three best docked complexes were imported to the workspace after setting the working directory as necessary and pre-processing of the protein was carried out by gauging the structural errors and refining them. The interaction complexes were optimized by minimizing via steepest descent algorithm for 500 times, and removing the waters as required. The environment for 100ns simulation was then set up using the system builder option in Maestro. Solvent model used was TIP3P and the boundary box for the complexes was defined by utilizing an orthorhombic box that constricts the complexes to 5 Å at each x, y and z axis to simulate the complexes within the containment box. The entire system was then neutralized by the appending of chlorine and sodium ions, but also any other ions depending on the total charge the system possesses. From literature study, it was identified that the approximate pH of the mid-gut of A. aegypti prior to blood feeding was found to be 6.0. Since it is at this point that the mosquito must be interceded from carrying out further operations such as feeding, the simulation was set to run at this pH, by altering the PropKA value in Desmond software. Since 50ns simulations are considered to provide good results, but not very conclusive on the complex stability, simulations were carried out at 100ns in the present project to ensure the robustness of the simulations. The trajectory recording interval was set to 0.1ns and normal pressure temperature (NPT) was selected with temperature set to 310K as the thermodynamic parameters for simulation.

steps.title: Identify Reference Proteome
steps.instruction: Retrieve the reference proteome for Aedes aegypti from the UniProt database.

substeps.instruction: Use Taxonomic ID 7159 (UniProt ID UP000008820).
Reference strain: LVP_AGWG (Genome assembly/annotation GCA_002204515.1 from EnsemblMetazoa).

steps.title: Select and Retrieve Protein Targets
steps.instruction: Identify and download sequences for 20 categories of protein targets based on literature and circadian rhythm expression.

substeps.instruction: Cross-check shortlisted proteins with published microarray data to verify expression during the circadian cycle.
Retrieve sequences for the 20 categories in FASTA format from UniProt using batch mode.
Filter sequences to prioritize complete sequences; use fragmented sequences only if complete ones are unavailable.

steps.title: Perform Sequence Alignment and Domain Analysis
steps.instruction: Assess sequence similarity and identify conserved domains to select representative proteins for modelling.

substeps.instruction: Perform Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA) using the MUSCLE algorithm in MEGA-X software.
Conduct conserved domain analysis using the NCBI Conserved Domain search tool (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Structure/bwrpsb/bwrpsb.cgi).
Submit query sequences in batch mode against the CDD-58235 position specific scoring matrices database.
Set parameters: composition corrected scoring, expected threshold value of 0.01, and maximum 500 hits.

steps.title: Model 3D Protein Structures
steps.instruction: Generate 3D models for the identified protein targets (309 proteins total) using a standalone RaptorX installation.

substeps.instruction: Install NR (non-redundant) database, template database, and PDB files.
Run 'buildFeature' to generate protein query sequence features.
Align target sequences to templates using 'CNFalign' (lite, fast, or normal versions).
Search for similar templates using the 'CNFsearch' package.
Predict query proteins using 'build3Dmodel' and generate 3D models via 'buildTopModels'.
Validate the resulting PDB files.

steps.title: Prepare Ligands and Controls
steps.instruction: Prepare natural bioactive ligands and synthetic controls for docking using the POAP command line.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve 3D structures of natural bioactives in .sdf format from NCBI PubChem.
Include positive controls (DEET, icardin, IR3535, and permethrin) and negative controls (ethanol and acetone).
Run ligand preparation via 'bash POAP_lig.bash -s' with a maximum of 64 parallel jobs.
Optimize ligands using the Merck molecular force field and generate 10 conformations via weighted rotor search.
Minimize the best conformer using the steepest descent algorithm for 100 steps.
Apply fixed parameters: vander waal’s cut-off distance (6 nm), convergence criteria (1e-6), electrostatic cut-off distance (10 Å), and non-bonded pair frequency (10).
Append hydrogen atoms to obtain final ligands in .pdbqt format.

steps.title: Prepare Proteins and Grid Boxes
steps.instruction: Prepare protein macromolecules for docking using AutoDock 4.2.6.

substeps.instruction: Add Gasteiger charges to atoms and merge non-polar hydrogens.
Redistribute partial charges and save macromolecules in .pdbqt format.
Generate grid boxes covering the entire protein molecule and record x, y, and z coordinates in a .txt configuration file.
Set the number of docking modes to 9.

steps.title: Perform Virtual Screening
steps.instruction: Execute multiple protein-multiple ligand docking using the POAP software with AutoDock Vina.

substeps.instruction: Run the virtual screening via 'bash POAP_vs.bash -s' in the terminal.
Provide paths for prepared ligands and proteins.
Set exhaustiveness to 50.

steps.title: Analyze Molecular Dynamics Simulations
steps.instruction: Perform 100ns simulations on the top docked complexes to validate stability.

substeps.instruction: Calculate Root Mean Square Deviation (RMSD) for 1000 frames within the trajectory to analyze stability.
Calculate Root Mean Square Fluctuation (RMSF) for both protein and ligand to analyze conformational changes.
Analyze protein-ligand contacts, amino acid residue interactions over the 100ns timeframe, hydrophobic bonds, hydrogen bonds, water bridges, and ionic bonds.
